summary: Long-lived SSE connections receiving 429s after enabling per-route shaping - request for SSE exemption/burst pool guidance
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightSensor reports increased 429 throttles on long-lived server-sent events (SSE) connections after enabling per-route shaping to isolate webhook traffic from background bulk jobs. Impact: customer-facing stream disruptions and elevated error counts in their UI; some customers see reconnection storms. Environment: Dedicated pool, prod us-east, tenant uses subaccount tokens and separates traffic via route regex patterns (/api/v1/streams/* and /api/v1/bulk/*).

Expected behavior: Long-lived SSE connections should be accounted under a long-lived connection bucket and only incur occasional keepalive token accounting, not the same burst window as short-lived request/response flows.

Actual behavior: After per-route shaping flag toggle, SSE connections begin receiving 429s roughly 5-10 minutes after start; logs show token-window depletion tied to per-route refill that assumes short request lifetime. Workaround attempted: customer increased per-route burst config and temporarily disabled shaping which reduced 429s but is not acceptable long term.

Request: Guidance on configuring a dedicated "long-lived connection exemption" or separate burst pool for keepalive/SSE paths on Dedicated deployments; recommended config values for burst credits, refill windows, and console dashboard queries to monitor stability.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Tenant on Dedicated pool with per-route shaping enabled (route weights: stream=0.5, bulk=0.5).
2) Open a long-lived SSE connection to /api/v1/streams/events?v=1 (client sends heartbeat every 20s).
3) Simulate occasional background bulk uploads to /api/v1/bulk/upload concurrently.
4) Observe metrics: route token bucket for /api/v1/streams shows steady drain; connection receives 429 after 6-8 minutes as refill window misaligns with long-lived session accounting.
5) Disable per-route shaping as temporary mitigation - 429s drop but route isolation lost.
logs: 2026-03-10T13:05:12.834Z [rate-limiter] tenant=brightsensor subaccount=ingest route=/api/v1/streams events=KEEPALIVE tokens_remaining=0 refill_window=60s
customer_notes: We only started seeing this after splitting traffic by route; previously long SSE connections were stable.
We rely on long-lived streams for real-time telemetry; reconnect storms cause downstream processing backlog and user-facing errors.
Willing to apply console config changes or feature flags but need safe guidance and recommended thresholds.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: per-route shaping created a smaller per-route refill window and a lower effective burst credit for the streams route; SSE keepalives are being counted as frequent small requests and depleting the bucket.
Checked dedicated-pool autoscaler logs - no scale events correlated with the first 429s.

Dashboard query: rate_limiter.tokens_remaining_by_route{tenant='brightsensor',route='streams'} shows sawtooth pattern with refill aligned to route-level epoch (60s) - too coarse for steady keepalive traffic. Link: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/rl/tenant-brightsensor
Reviewed console config for route weights - streams had weight 0.5 and burst_capacity set to default for short-lived traffic.
support_actions: Escalated to SRE to verify rate-limiter accounting semantics for SSE vs short requests.
Applied ephemeral per-route bump to burst_capacity for streams (from default 100 -> 1000) for 1 hour; observed reduction in 429s during test window.
Recorded temporary mitigation and instructed customer to keep shaping disabled in the interim if critical.
comments: Ava Chen (Support) 2026-03-10: Initial ticket created after customer observed 429s; asked for logs and representative client ID.
BrightSensor - Jordan (Customer) 2026-03-10: Provided logs and confirmed pattern - SSE 429s start after ~6m and sometimes trigger client reconnect backoff. We're on a Dedicated lease (monthly).

Mateo Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-11: Hypothesis - per-route refill windows are optimized for short RPCs; recommend creating separate rate class for long-lived connections with larger burst and longer refill window. Will validate on staging.

Mateo Ruiz (SRE) 2026-03-11: Ran controlled test - increased burst_capacity on streams route and introduced keepalive exemption that charges 1 token per 60s rather than per packet; 0 429s observed for 30m test. Need product sign-off for persistent config.
Product Ops - Lina Park 2026-03-12: Needs documented guidance + console UI affordance to configure 'connection class' for routes. Flagging as follow-up product request.
recommended_resolution: Short term: Apply a per-route 'long-lived' rate class on BrightSensor tenant with burst_capacity=1200 and refill_window=300s for /api/v1/streams and set keepalive token charge to 1 token per 60s. Monitoring for 24 hours.
Medium term: Add console template for 'SSE/long-lived' route profile (UI toggle + suggested defaults) and allow dedicated pools to create small dedicated burst pools for realtime lanes.

Long term: Update rate-limiter to support connection-aware accounting (charge per-connection-period vs per-packet) and add a preflight detector to suggest exemptions when console detects steady keepalive patterns.
resolution_notes: Temporary per-route burst bump applied and verified; pending product work for a reusable console profile. Customer agreed to keep shaping off until we roll out a safe config. Follow-up ticket created for product: INT-20721.
resolution: Mitigated (temporary config applied) - awaiting product change for permanent solution
next_steps: 1) Schedule cross-team sync (Support, SRE, Product) to scope console 'SSE profile' and rollout plan — target owner Lina Park.
2) Create product engineering story (INT-20721) to implement connection-aware accounting and console template.
3) Monitor tenant metrics for 72 hours and confirm no regression post-shaping re-enable.
